title: Report on Studying at Lund University
paragraphs: For two months, April and May, I did clerkships in the ICU and internal medicine at Lund University. Before the destination was decided, I vaguely thought it would probably be Lund University among the partner schools, so I had made friends with the Lund University students who came to Nagoya University. In Sweden there is a culture of fika, a coffee break, and it is regarded as very important. In both departments there was such a time of about 30 minutes, separate from lunchtime.

ICU. I do not remember the number of doctors because it was large, but there were eight beds. Let me introduce a basic day in the ICU. There is a conference from 7:30 in the morning. There, information is shared about what happened the night before and about new patients. After that there are rounds, in which the condition of each patient is checked. Each time, I was assigned two patients. As soon as rounds were over, I took in the information from the charts in detail. What was hard here was that the charts were in Swedish, so I had to have the supervising doctor translate them. Then, at 11:30 there is a smaller conference, where I presented on my patients and received feedback. In the afternoon, time passed observing the emergency department and discussing with local students, and at the 16:00 conference we handed over to the night shift team and finished. The conferences were held in English for my sake. The atmosphere was friendly and it was very enjoyable.

Internal medicine. The hospital was in a town called Ystad, one hour by train from Lund. There was a conference every day from 8 a.m., but it was all in Swedish and I could not understand the meaning. After that, together with local students I took the pre-visit histories of outpatients, did physical examinations and wrote the charts. I also did ward rounds with the supervising doctor and students, and each time they taught me various things. The clerkship usually ended at 15:00 or 16:00. The trains were often late, so commuting by train was a little hard.

Dormitory life. It was a dormitory for 28 people in total, with a shared kitchen, toilet and shower. The dormitory was one where university and graduate students studying abroad in various fields at Lund University from all over the world gathered. Interacting with people with various backgrounds was a lot of fun. It was good that we could help each other when in trouble.

Leisure. On weekdays I basically played tennis after the clerkship. It was very good because the daylight hours were long and there were many free tennis courts. I made trips around Sweden, going around visiting friends I had made in Japan. Since my time abroad happened to be festival season, I also took part in festivals on holidays. Of course, I also traveled to other European countries.
Finally, I would like to express my gratitude to everyone, beginning with Dr. 粕谷 and Dr. 長谷川, who supported my exchange study abroad.
